name: Card Effect DSL
description: The interpreter that turns card data into game verbs. A card is a row of data — cost, target rule, an ordered list of effect steps with triggers — and this component walks the row and dispatches each step onto utility.command_bus instead of hard-coding card behavior, because a deckbuilder lives or dies on how fast a designer can ship a card without touching engine code. It owns parsing, cost validation, and target resolution. It does not own the numbers: damage steps are handed to combat.damage_resolver, status steps to combat.status_effects, and energy payment is checked against combat.energy_per_turn before the first step fires — a card that cannot be paid for is rejected whole, never half-resolved, because partial resolution is where card-game bugs breed.

inputs.name: targetModes
inputs.description: Which targeting rules cards may declare. Restricting the list is a design tool: a set with no 'ally' targeting reads very differently at the deckbuilding screen.

inputs.name: allowChainedTriggers
inputs.description: Whether effects triggered mid-resolution may themselves trigger further effects. Off by default: unbounded chains are where card games go to become un-debuggable.

inputs.name: maxStepsPerCard
inputs.description: Hard cap on effect steps in one card. A guardrail against malformed data, not a design budget — real cards rarely need more than three.

outputs.name: lastResolvedCard
outputs.description: The card id, paid cost, chosen targets, and per-step outcomes of the most recent play — the full replay record.

outputs.name: cardsRejected
outputs.description: Lifetime count of plays refused for cost, target, or legality. A rising count is a UI problem, not a rules problem.
